title: Signal Fusion Gateway for PagerDuty & Slack Enriched Summaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'Signal Fusion Gateway' service that aggregates signals (trace snippets, metric deltas, log excerpts, recent error rates, and runbook pointers) into a compact enriched summary attached to PagerDuty incidents and Slack alert threads. The gateway will: 1) ingest webhook payloads from our existing alerting pipeline, 2) call tracing hooks and telemetry stores to stitch context, 3) render a size-bounded summary (text + key-value metadata + 1-2 relevant links), and 4) POST back to PagerDuty and Slack using curated templates. Goal is to reduce on-call MTTI and context-swim time by surfacing the most relevant runtime signals and a single-click runbook entry point.
scope: In scope: gateway service, PagerDuty webhook enrichment, Slack message attachments, trace snippet extraction (sampled), metric snapshotting for the last 5m, concise runbook link resolver, basic rate limiting and templating. Out of scope: automated remediation, full incident timeline replay, deep ML summarization beyond heuristics.
solution_proposal: Implement a small stateless service (Go) deployed in the observability namespace. On incoming alert webhook, the gateway will: (a) normalize the alert, (b) query the trace-store for the top 2 spans by error count in the last 2 minutes, (c) fetch metric summaries (p95 latency, error-rate %), (d) run a templated heuristics engine to pick 3 contextual lines from logs (using log search with time-window filters), (e) build a 4-line human-readable summary + 4 KV fields (service, endpoint, p95, error-rate), and (f) attach to PD incident via PD Events API and post a threaded Slack message with actions (open runbook, open traces, mute alert). Use existing auth & secrets (KMS) and respect tenancy and tenant-scoped routing for Dedicated/Private customers.
data_model: All gateway payloads are opaque JSON strings when stored. Normalized summary schema: 'summary_text' (string), 'service' (string), 'endpoint' (string), 'p95_ms' (string), 'error_rate_pct' (string), 'trace_ids' (list of strings), 'links' (list of strings), 'timestamp' (ISO string). Stored in the alerts-summaries S3 prefix for 30 days for attach/replay. No PII accepted; gateway rejects alerts flagged PII at ingestion.
integration_points: Runbook registry (confluence://runbooks or drive link resolver)
acceptance_criteria: When a PD alert arrives, an enriched summary is attached to the incident within 8s for 90% of synthetic tests
Summary contains no more than 280 characters of human text and includes 3 metadata KV fields and at least one actionable link
Slack alerts receive a threaded enrichment message with runbook and open-trace links (tests in #oncall-staging pass)
Gateway respects per-tenant rate limits and fails open (no blocking) when trace-store is slow
End-to-end test harness (integration) added to observability CI with synthetic alert generator
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Gateway could add latency to incident creation. Mitigation: attach enrichment asynchronously within a 10s window; PD incident created immediately with 'enrichment pending' notice.
Risk: Sensitive data included in summaries. Mitigation: reuse existing PII flags from alert pipeline; default redact; security review required.
Risk: Spike in PD/Slack API usage. Mitigation: implement batching/backoff and exponential retry; circuit breaker to stop attachments under sustained failures.
Risk: False signals reduce trust. Mitigation: conservative heuristics, prioritise traces with error tags and high span durations; expose opt-out via alert labels.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for normalization/templating 2) Integration tests using the synthetic alert generator to assert summary shape and latency 3) Staging run in #oncall-staging with canary traffic (1% of alerts) 4) Chaos test: simulate trace-store timeout and assert gateway fails open 5) Security review checklist for PII redaction and credential handling

Add Prometheus metrics (enrichment_latency_ms, attach_failures_total) and dashboard tile
